name: Tyler Satchel Orden
body:
Statement. Erdős problem #112: k(n,m) is the least k such that every oriented graph on k vertices has n pairwise non-adjacent vertices or a transitive tournament on m vertices. This submission gives new lower bounds for four small cases.

What was known. k(7,3) >= 37, k(8,3) >= 46, k(6,4) >= 65 and k(3,6) >= 68, from circulants in the GitHub repository rsvaultpudgy-create/erdos-112-lower-bounds (single commit, 11 Nov 2026, described by its owner as AI-generated and unrefereed). Upper bounds for m = 3: k(7,3) <= 45 and k(8,3) <= 59, from k(n,3) <= n^2 - n + 3 (Ihringer, Rajendraprasad and Weinert, Discrete Math. 2021).

My results. k(7,3) >= 39, k(8,3) >= 47, k(6,4) >= 78 and k(3,6) >= 71. Upper bounds are not improved.

Witnesses (each is an oriented graph on N vertices with no independent n-set and no transitive m-tournament, so k(n,m) >= N + 1):
k(7,3) >= 39: bicirculant on Z_19 x {0,1}, vertex (x,i) numbered 19i + x, arc (x,i) -> (x+s mod 19, j) for s in S_ij: S_00 = {5,6,16,17}, S_01 = {16,17}, S_10 = {5,6}, S_11 = {10,11,16,17}. 38 vertices, 228 arcs.
k(8,3) >= 47: bicirculant on Z_23 x {0,1}, vertex (x,i) numbered 23i + x: S_00 = {2,5,11,19}, S_01 = {4,10,18}, S_10 = {0,8,17}, S_11 = {2,11,19,20}. 46 vertices, 322 arcs.
k(6,4) >= 78: circulant on Z_77, arc x -> x+s for s in {3,11,14,19,20,22,30,35,36,40,44,46,52,64,68,75}. 77 vertices, 1232 arcs.
k(3,6) >= 71: circulant on Z_70, arc x -> x+s for s in {1,2,7,8,14,15,16,17,21,24,26,29,30,32,37,39,45,47,48,52,60,61,64}. 70 vertices, 1610 arcs. (A second witness on Z_69 gives k(3,6) >= 70.)

How to check. The Zenodo record has the arc lists and two separately written checkers (C and plain Python, no libraries); "sh run_checks.sh" rebuilds every graph from its connection sets and checks it in a few seconds, with negative controls and three published graphs as positive controls.
Lean: all four bounds are proved in Lean 4 (no sorry, no native_decide; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound), on the same definitions as my Palomar-registered proof of 30 <= k(6,3) <= 32.
